\section[bañarse]{bañarse — to have a swim; to have a bath}

\label{lesson:ES-C690-banarse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the marsh, then the Spanish for the cliff.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: bañarse}
\textbf{bañarse} — \textquotedblleft{}to have a swim; to have a bath\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Nos bañamos en el mar por la mañana.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We swim in the sea in the morning.}
\end{quote}

At the beach, \emph{bañarse} is to go in the water, not to swim lengths.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bañarse} is built on \emph{baño} \textquotedblleft{}bath\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{balneum} \textquotedblleft{}a bath\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bañarse}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bañarse}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bañarse}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the marsh, then the Spanish for the cliff, then say \emph{bañarse} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does bañarse mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To have a swim; to have a bath\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[broncearse]{broncearse — to get a tan}

\label{lesson:ES-C690-broncearse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the cliff, then the Spanish for to have a swim.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: broncearse}
\textbf{broncearse} — \textquotedblleft{}to get a tan\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Me bronceo muy rápido.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I tan very quickly.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Estar bronceado} — to be tanned.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{broncearse} is built on \emph{bronce} \textquotedblleft{}bronze\textquotedblright{}, which was borrowed from Italian \emph{bronzo} (EtymDB): tanned skin turns the colour of bronze.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{broncearse}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{broncearse}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{broncearse}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the cliff, then the Spanish for to have a swim, then say \emph{broncearse} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does broncearse mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To get a tan\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la sombrilla]{la sombrilla — the sunshade, the beach umbrella}

\label{lesson:ES-C690-sombrilla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to have a swim, then the Spanish for to get a tan.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la sombrilla}
\textbf{la sombrilla} — \textquotedblleft{}the sunshade, the beach umbrella\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ponemos la sombrilla cerca del agua.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We put the sunshade up near the water.}
\end{quote}

\emph{El paraguas} is for rain; \emph{la sombrilla} is for sun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sombrilla} is a little \emph{sombra} \textquotedblleft{}shade\textquotedblright{}. The origin of \emph{sombra} is not settled; it is often linked to Latin \emph{umbra} \textquotedblleft{}shade\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la sombrilla}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la sombrilla}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la sombrilla}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to have a swim, then the Spanish for to get a tan, then say \emph{la sombrilla} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la sombrilla mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The sunshade, the beach umbrella\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[el bañador]{el bañador — the swimsuit, the swimming trunks}

\label{lesson:ES-C690-banador}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to get a tan, then the Spanish for the sunshade.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el bañador}
\textbf{el bañador} — \textquotedblleft{}the swimsuit, the swimming trunks\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No olvides el bañador.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Do not forget your swimsuit.}
\end{quote}

A Spain word; Latin America says \emph{el traje de baño}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bañador} is built on \emph{bañar} \textquotedblleft{}to bathe\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{baño} \textquotedblleft{}bath\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Latin \emph{balneum}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to get a tan, then the Spanish for the sunshade, then say \emph{el bañador} again

\section[tumbarse]{tumbarse — to lie down}

\label{lesson:ES-C690-tumbarse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the sunshade, then the Spanish for the swimsuit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: tumbarse}
\textbf{tumbarse} — \textquotedblleft{}to lie down\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Me tumbo en la arena a leer.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I lie down on the sand to read.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Estar tumbado} — to be lying down.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tumbarse} is built on \emph{tumbar} \textquotedblleft{}to knock down\textquotedblright{}, which is usually taken to imitate the thud of something falling; the origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
